description: First golden fixture for OCaml (#6812) — until this landed, NOTHING about internal/extractors/ocaml was graded. Three files carry the constructs the `inherit` question turns on: `inherit` inside `object ... end` at a class declaration (shapes.ml), `inherit` inside a class TYPE and the module-level `include`/`open` that look like it and are not it (containers.ml), and `inherit` inside an `object ... end` nested in a `let` BODY (render.ml) — the one context where the keyword is reachable by the CALLS scanner today, and therefore the only one this fixture can grade in both directions. HIERARCHY IS DELIBERATELY UNGRADED. OCaml emits no EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS (#6370 group (a)); this fixture asserts no hierarchy row in EITHER direction for the object/class-type forms, so it does not repeat the erlang-otp-mini trap of pinning a missing edge as correct. It does forbid the shapes that are NOT inheritance in any OCaml — a module `include` becoming a hierarchy edge — because those stay forbidden after #6370's OCaml arm lands. ONE PRINCIPLE GOVERNS EVERY ROW HERE, applied in both directions after a review found it applied in neither: a row is kept only if it has been DEMONSTRATED capable of firing, by a mutant, and dropped otherwise. That is why all six forbidden relationships and both forbidden entities carry a FIRES verdict with the mutant named, including the three future-facing hierarchy fences that were originally argued to be unfireable and were in fact merely mis-dialected; and it is why ten of nineteen subtype assertions were dropped as redundant while `make_logger`/`make_counter` keep theirs — those two are the `let x = object … end` pair a CST-backed producer could genuinely reclassify, so the assertion distinguishes something. “Aimed at a future producer” is a reason to write a row, never a reason to skip demonstrating that it works. Known divergences present in the source and deliberately NOT asserted, so nobody reads their absence as approval: the functor `module Make (C : Comparable) = struct` is not extracted at all (moduleRE requires `=`/`:` immediately after the name, and a parameter list intervenes); no `class`/`class type`/`method`/`val` construct produces any entity, so shape/circle/square/printer/stream_writer are invisible; indented `let`s inside a module body are not extracted, which also means module CONTAINS is empty here; and every module in containers.ml reports the SAME end line, which is the depth-walker defect measured in the PR that added this fixture.

expected_entities.name: point
expected_entities.note: Top-level record type. Baseline non-object extraction in the file that holds the object cases, so a regression that killed shapes.ml wholesale is distinguishable from one that only touched objects.

expected_entities.name: bounds
expected_entities.note: SECOND type in the same file: typeRE de-duplicates by name, and a fixture with one type per file cannot tell 'types work' from 'the first type works'.

expected_entities.name: level
expected_entities.note: A variant type rather than a record — the type-declaration RHS varies while the position (column 0) is held constant.

expected_entities.name: shapes.ml
expected_entities.note: The file entity is the carrier of the IMPORTS edge for `open Printf` — OCaml anchors imports on the file, not on a module entity, so without this row the import assertions below have no from endpoint to name.

expected_entities.name: Comparable
expected_entities.note: `module type Comparable = sig ... end` — the `module type` arm of moduleRE, and the only entity here whose body is a `sig` rather than a `struct`.

expected_entities.name: Base
expected_entities.note: A plain `module ... = struct`. Target of the `include` in Extended.

expected_entities.name: Extended
expected_entities.note: The module that `include`s another. It must exist as a module and must NOT gain a hierarchy edge — see forbidden_relationships.

expected_entities.name: render_with
expected_entities.note: Declared AFTER two `class type ... object ... end` blocks. A let-extractor whose column-0 anchor were loosened, or whose scan were confused by the intervening `object`/`end` keywords, loses this one first.

expected_entities.name: make_logger
expected_entities.note: #6812 CENTRAL ROW: a `let` whose body IS an `object ... end` containing `inherit`. This is the only context in the fixture where the `inherit` line is inside a scanned body, and therefore the only one where over-firing on the keyword is observable.

expected_entities.name: make_counter
expected_entities.note: #6812 NEGATIVE CONTROL for the row above: the same `let x = object ... end` shape with NO `inherit`. Holds the object nesting constant and varies only the presence of the keyword.

expected_entities.name: append_all
expected_entities.note: #6812 identifier hazard, the NON-triggering half: `end` here is followed by `_`, and Go treats `_` as a word character, so `\bend\b` re-run against the remaining slice does NOT match inside `end_all`. Paired with `backend` and `legend` below, which do end at a word boundary and do match. Stated this precisely because an earlier version spelled all three with a trailing `_word`, so the axis it claimed to vary contained only this case. NOT GRADED by an assertion: nothing in this fixture asserts a module span, and the hazard only reaches extractModuleBody, so these three put both outcomes in the corpus rather than fencing either.

expected_entities.name: backend
expected_entities.note: #6812 identifier hazard, the TRIGGERING half: `backend` ends at a word boundary, so the slice-relative `\bend\b` matches and the scanner reads a closing keyword inside an identifier. Also the target of a forbidden CALLS row, which is what makes the name itself load-bearing rather than decorative.

expected_entities.name: legend
expected_entities.note: #6812 identifier hazard, triggering, second spelling: `legend` differs from `backend` in everything but the trailing `end`, so a fix keyed on one word does not pass by accident. Two triggering names and one non-triggering name is the whole axis.

expected_relationships.note: #6812 THE ROW THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR. `inherit stream_writer prefix` inside make_logger's object body. The PARENT NAME survives extraction today — but only as a CALLS edge from the enclosing function, because the extractor has no class vocabulary and `inherit` itself is suppressed as a keyword. Recording it as CALLS is not an endorsement: it is the measurement of what the regex path currently produces, which the owner's #6812 comment requires be enumerated BEFORE any grammar swap replaces it. When #6370's OCaml arm lands, this row is the evidence of what the swap must not silently drop.

The only row in the fixture whose TO side resolves to a real entity rather than a bare name, so a regression that stopped binding CALLS targets to entities is distinguishable from one that stopped emitting CALLS at all.

The module-qualified call form (callDotRE) rather than the bare form. Emitted from the body of the function whose NAME contains the substring the block scanner treats as a closing keyword — if that hazard ever truncates the body, this row goes first.

#6812: `open Printf` is an IMPORT. The whole question this fixture serves is whether the module-composition keywords stay distinct from inheritance, and this is the row that pins the one of them that IS an edge today.

#6812: `open List` in the same file as `include Base`. Paired with the forbidden `Extended -> Base` rows: `open` produces an edge, `include` must not produce a hierarchy one. A fixture carrying only one of the two keywords cannot tell a producer that handles both apart from one that handles neither.

A member of the object make_counter returns. Held as an EXPECTED row here and as a FORBIDDEN row from make_logger: the same identifier must be reachable from its own function and unreachable from the previous one, which is what makes the let-body boundary graded in both directions rather than one.

forbidden_relationships.note: #6812 OVER-FIRING, the keyword itself: `inherit` sits in ocamlKeywords (extractor.go:99) as one of ~60 CALLS-blocklist entries. FIRES, verified: deleting the `"inherit": true` entry produces exactly this edge, because callBareRE matches `inherit ` in make_logger's object body. This is the row that makes the keyword suppression graded rather than incidental — before this fixture, removing that entry broke nothing.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, body boundary: `bump` is a method of the NEXT function's object (make_counter), one top-level declaration further down. FIRES, verified: deleting the `break` in extractLetBody (extractor.go:401) makes make_logger's body run to end-of-file and produces this edge. Paired with the expected `make_counter -> bump` row, so a producer that over-reaches is distinguishable from one that under-reaches.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, body boundary, second hop: `backend` is TWO top-level declarations past make_logger. FIRES under the same mutant as the row above, and is stated with a RESOLVED to side rather than a bare one on purpose — `bump` is a method name that binds to nothing, `backend` is a top-level function that binds to an entity, so the two rows also grade the forbidden matcher on both of its target dialects. A single row written the other way round would have been silently unfireable: to_bare_name only matches an edge whose target stayed a raw string, which this one does not.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, `include` is not inheritance: `include Base` splices a module's contents into Extended. It is module composition, not a class-inheritance edge, and it stays forbidden after #6370's OCaml arm lands — which is why this row is safe to write while the object-form hierarchy edge is deliberately left ungraded. FIRES, verified: a mutant emitting Extended --[EXTENDS]--> Base from the `include` produces exactly this hit. Written with to_bare_name first, it was SILENTLY UNFIREABLE — Base is a top-level module that binds to an entity, so an edge to it carries a RESOLVED target and to_bare_name can never match it; the mutant emitted the edge and the fence reported zero. The reason then given for the non-firing, that OCaml has no hierarchy vocabulary to mutate, was an argument rather than a demonstration, and it was wrong: the cause was the target dialect, and on the day #6370's arm emits this edge both fences would have passed.

#6812 OVER-FIRING: the same claim in the other hierarchy kind. Written separately because a producer that emits IMPLEMENTS where it means EXTENDS passes a fence naming only one of them — the exact confusion the #6370 audit found languages sitting on either side of. FIRES, verified with its OWN mutant emitting IMPLEMENTS rather than EXTENDS, because a fence verified only through its sibling is a fence verified once.

#6812 OVER-FIRING, cross-construct: `class type verbose_printer = object inherit printer ... end` sits in the same file as `module type Comparable = sig ... end`. A producer that finds `inherit` by searching a file rather than by anchoring inside a block binds it to whichever `module`/`class` declaration it last saw — and moduleRE's last match in this file is Comparable's sibling set, not a class. This is the one hierarchy fence that KEEPS to_bare_name, and deliberately: `printer` is a `class type` and produces no entity at all, so an edge to it can only ever carry a raw string and a resolved to-side could never match. FIRES, verified with a mutant emitting Comparable --[EXTENDS]--> printer. The pairing with the two rows above is the point — the same fence is unfireable in one dialect and unfireable in the other, depending on whether the target binds, so the dialect has to be chosen per row and demonstrated per row.

forbidden_entities.name: inherit
forbidden_entities.note: #6812: the keyword must never be promoted to an entity of its own. FIRES, verified: a mutant appending a SCOPE.Operation named `inherit` to extractOCaml's output produces exactly one forbidden entity hit, exit 2. Its earlier note claimed it was unreachable because nothing in extractOCaml creates an entity from a CALLS target — true of today's code and irrelevant to whether the ROW works, which is the only thing a fence's note should assert. Aimed at a grammar-backed producer, where an `inherit` CST node IS a node and naming it directly is the obvious slip.

forbidden_entities.name: object
forbidden_entities.note: #6812: `object` opens a block and is not a type. FIRES, verified with its own mutant appending a SCOPE.Component named `object`, scored separately from the row above because two fences verified by one mutant are one verification. Aimed at the producer that replaces this extractor.
